function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning: The user wants to find two movie theaters near San Diego that have showtimes: 5pm for "Tenet" (天能) and 7:30pm for "007生死交戰" (which is "No Time To Die"). They want to find two theaters that provide those showtimes. We need to use the function find_movie_showing. The function signature expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? Actually we need to find two theaters. We can call the function with location "San Diego, CA", movie "Tenet", time ["17:00"] to get theaters showing Tenet at 5pm. Then call with movie "No Time To Die", time ["19:30"] to get theaters showing that at 7:30pm. But the function returns any. We need to call it. The user wants two theaters that provide both showtimes? Or two separate theaters: one for Tenet at 5pm, one for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. The phrasing: "尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。" Means "Find two movie theaters near San Diego that offer 5pm show of Tenet and 7:30pm show of No Time To Die." It could mean find two theaters that each have those showtimes? Or find two theaters that collectively have those showtimes? Likely they want two theaters that each have those showtimes. But the function only returns theaters for a given movie and time. We can call it twice and combine results. Let's call find_movie_showing twice.
